name: FortiGate — Lateral Movement: Admin-Protocol Fan-Out from Non-Admin Host
description:
Attacker objective
Spread across internal hosts via administrative protocols (SMB/RDP/WinRM/SSH/RPC/VNC) after an initial compromise.

Attack logic
Fan-out to many internal hosts over administrative protocols is normally limited to sanctioned management/jump hosts and domain controllers. A source outside that set reaching many internal hosts on admin ports is anomalous lateral movement.

Why this detection works
Excluding the management subnet, domain controllers and scanners, then counting distinct internal destinations on admin ports, isolates genuine east-west fan-out.

False positives
A new legitimate jump/management/backup/patch host.

Tuning
Add verified management systems to the exclusion after review.

Required telemetry
FortiGate traffic logs (source.ip, destination.ip, destination.port, action).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. source.ip = the fanning-out host; the ports/destinations show the spread.
2. Correlate with a prior malware / DNS-C2 / exploit alert on the source — lateral movement follows initial access.
3. Isolate if confirmed.
query: fortinet.firewall.srccountry:"Reserved" and fortinet.firewall.dstcountry:"Reserved" and fortinet.firewall.action:"accept" and destination.port:(445 or 3389 or 5985 or 5986 or 22 or 135 or 5900) and not source.ip:("192.168.166.1" or "192.168.25.1" or "192.168.25.2" or "172.17.25.1" or "192.168.157.1" ) and not source.ip:"192.168.41.0/24"
